field_guide.cik: Company identifier stored as text. Join filings using both CIK and accession number.
field_guide.fact_name: Raw XBRL concept. Related concepts may have different definitions.
field_guide.fact_category: Taxonomy namespace. Compare concepts only under compatible definitions.
field_guide.fact_value: Value in the returned unit. NULL is missing and never implies zero.
field_guide.unit: Original units. USD values are unscaled dollars.
field_guide.end_date: Fact period end. It can precede the filing's fiscal year.
field_guide.fiscal_year: Fiscal-year label of the disclosure. Verify the fact's actual end_date.
field_guide.fiscal_period: Source fiscal-period label. Check period length and frame for flows.
field_guide.frame: Supplementary period indicator. A missing frame does not establish annual duration.
field_guide.filed_date: Submission date, distinct from the fact period end.
field_guide.form_type: Source filing form. One period may be disclosed in several filings.
field_guide.accession_number: SEC submission identifier. A matching filings row may be absent.
field_guide.dimension_segment: Segment scope if supplied. Absence alone does not prove comparability.
field_guide.dimension_geography: Geographic scope if supplied. Absence alone does not prove comparability.

The commercial markets for these vaccines are seasonal and characterized, particularly in the U.S. (our largest market), by a fragmented customer base, unpredictability in orders and seasonality of deliveries. As the SARS-CoV-2 virus continues to evolve, Spikevax continues to be a key tool in fighting COVID-19. As part of our strategy to continue to combat COVID-19, we develop and assess variant-specific versions of our COVID vaccine. In August and September 2024, we received regulatory approvals in major markets for our updated COVID vaccine, targeting the JN.1 (mRNA-1273.167) and KP.2 (mRNA-1273.712) subvariants of SARS-CoV-2, based on the new variant composition requests from different public health bodies. We developed JN.1 and KP.2 formulations of mRNA-1273 in accordance with regulatory guidance, with the goal of broadening vaccine-induced immunity and providing protection against circulating SARS-CoV-2 variants. We have also observed preliminary clinical trial data showing that these vaccines generate a robust immune response (cross-neutralization) against currently circulating variants of SARS-CoV-2.

We have two commercial respiratory virus vaccines—Spikevax (our COVID vaccine) and mRESVIA (our RSV vaccine for older adults). Additionally, we have achieved four positive Phase 3 data readouts for our next-generation COVID vaccine (mRNA-1283), our RSV vaccine for high-risk adults aged 18 to 59 (mRNA-1345), our seasonal flu+COVID vaccine (mRNA-1083), and our seasonal flu vaccine (mRNA-1010). We have a total of 15 respiratory programs in our current portfolio, summarized below.

Our COVID vaccine is our first commercial product and is marketed, where approved, under the name Spikevax®. Our original vaccine, mRNA-1273, targeted the SARS-CoV-2 ancestral strain, and we have leveraged our mRNA platform to rapidly adapt our vaccine to emerging SARS-CoV-2 strains to provide protection as the virus evolves and regulatory guidance is updated.

hits.text: Our first commercial product, Spikevax (our COVID-19 vaccine), has helped hundreds of millions of people worldwide combat COVID-19. SARS-CoV-2, the virus that causes COVID-19, continues to evolve and in 2023, the COVID-19 vaccine market transitioned to an endemic, seasonal commercial market. To adapt to the evolving market, we significantly resized our manufacturing infrastructure to help position our COVID-19 franchise for future profitability. We achieved 2023 net product sales of $6.7 billion, with $6.1 billion of COVID-19 vaccine sales, and recognition of approximately $0.6 billion of deferred revenue related to our efforts with Gavi, The Vaccine Alliance. In the United States, we achieved 48% market share in the retail market for the 2023 fall season, compared to 37% in the 2022 fall season.
•our expectations regarding the evolution of the endemic, commercial COVID-19 vaccine market and future demand for COVID-19 vaccines;

In the third quarter of 2023, we commenced sales of our latest COVID-19 vaccine to the U.S. commercial market, in addition to continuing sales to foreign governments and organizations. In the U.S., our COVID-19 vaccine is sold primarily to wholesalers and distributors, and to a lesser extent, directly to retailers and healthcare providers. Wholesalers and distributors typically do not make upfront payments to us.
hits.section: Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data

hits.text: Through 2023, our only approved product and sole source of product sales has been our COVID-19 vaccine. The global market is transitioning to an endemic, commercial market for COVID-19 vaccine sales, resulting in different market and production dynamics than during the pandemic, including a more fragmented customer base, less predictability in orders, greater seasonality of demand, increased distribution costs, and higher costs of goods sold. Furthermore, our assumptions regarding the product presentation that will be accepted or preferred by the market (e.g., single-dose presentation), which could vary by market, may prove incorrect. In addition, certain U.S. private vaccine market practices, including regarding discounts, rebates and returns, may cause us to realize significantly lower revenues than list prices. We may also be adversely affected by similar market practices outside of the United States.

Total revenue decreased by $12.4 billion, or 64%, in 2023, primarily attributable to a significant reduction in net product sales of our COVID-19 vaccine. Net product sales decreased by $11.8 billion, or 64%, in 2023, mainly due to lower sales volume across all regions in 2023, reflecting the market's transition to a seasonal commercial market for COVID-19 vaccine. The decline was partially offset by a higher average selling price, particularly in the United States, where commercial market sales commenced in the third quarter of 2023. Other revenue decreased by $651 million, or 79%, in 2023, mainly due to a decrease in grant revenue under our agreement with BARDA for the development of our COVID-19 vaccine, and lower collaboration revenue following the recognition of Merck's $250 million participation payment related to our INT collaboration in 2022.
hits.section: Item 7. MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

hits.text: With respect to our COVID-19 vaccine, although the U.S. and certain foreign governments have contractually agreed to indemnify us or make statutory immunity available to us, such indemnification or statutory immunity may be unavailable to cover potential claims or liabilities resulting from the research, development, manufacture, distribution or commercialization of the vaccine. Additionally, other foreign governments that we contract with may not provide us with similar contractual indemnity or statutory immunity, and we will not have the benefit of such indemnities or immunities in the future as the COVID-19 vaccine market transitions to a commercial market in the United States and elsewhere. Substantial claims arising from the vaccine outside the scope of or in excess of U.S. or foreign government indemnity or statutory immunity could harm our financial condition and operating results. Moreover, any adverse event or injury for which we are liable, even if fully covered under an indemnity or immunity, could negatively affect our reputation.

In addition to our internal manufacturing facilities, we also maintain relationships with CMOs in the United States and abroad, providing drug substance and fill-finish capacity for our vaccines. As noted above, during the third quarter of 2023, we resized our manufacturing footprint to reduce our commitments to certain CMOs as a result of lower anticipated demand for COVID-19 vaccines in the endemic market.

Prior to the third quarter of 2023, we sold our COVID-19 vaccine to the U.S. Government, foreign governments and organizations. The agreements and related amendments with these entities generally do not include variable consideration, such as discounts, rebates or returns. message.content: I have sufficient evidence. Let me compute the revenue changes.

**Moderna, Inc. (CIK 1682852) — Commercial dynamics and market share of its vaccines**

**1. Structural shift: pandemic → endemic, seasonal commercial market**
- Per the FY2023 10-K (report_end 2023-12-31, Item 1): "in 2023, the COVID-19 vaccine market transitioned to an endemic, seasonal commercial market." Through 2023 Spikevax was the only approved product and sole source of product sales.
- In Q3 2023 Moderna began selling to the **U.S. commercial market** (previously U.S. government/foreign government advance purchase agreements). U.S. sales go mainly to wholesalers/distributors, and to a lesser extent directly to retailers and providers; wholesalers typically make no upfront payments. The private market brings rebates, discounts and returns, so realized revenue can be well below list price (FY2023 10-K, Item 1A and Item 7).
- Per the FY2024 10-K (report_end 2024-12-31, Item 1): the markets are "seasonal and characterized, particularly in the U.S. (our largest market), by a fragmented customer base, unpredictability in orders and seasonality of deliveries." 2024 also made Moderna a **multi-product** company with approval of mRESVIA (RSV vaccine, adults ≥60).

**2. Market share evolution**
- **COVID (Spikevax):** In the U.S. retail market, Moderna reported **48% share for the 2023 fall season vs. 37% for the 2022 fall season** — a gain of ~11 percentage points (FY2023 10-K, Item 1, chunk 1682852/mrna-20231231:20438). In 2024 the trend reversed: the FY2024 10-K states "in 2024, our share of the COVID vaccine market declined due in part to increased commercial competition" (Item 1A, chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:212172). No specific 2024 share percentage is disclosed in the bundled reports.
- **RSV (mRESVIA):** Launched into a market already held by Pfizer and GSK, "who entered the U.S. market prior to us and achieved larger market shares in 2024"; Moderna did not participate in the full 2024 U.S. contracting season (FY2024 10-K, Item 1, chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:156829). Management's stated goal (a plan, not a result) is to increase U.S. share and global access with a full 2025 contracting season (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:28753).
- **Competitive set:** Pfizer/BioNTech (mRNA COVID), Sanofi and Novavax (COVID); Pfizer and GSK (RSV). Moderna also cites exclusion from many European markets due to a pandemic-era European Commission competitor contract, and competitor advantages in bundling, supply-chain scale and purchasing power (FY2024 10-K, Item 1A).

**3. Commercial/financial trajectory (disclosed values)**
- Net product sales: **$18.4B (2022) → $6.7B (2023) → $3.1B (2024)**, largely Spikevax (FY2024 10-K, Item 7, chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:416224). 2023 included ~$6.1B of COVID-19 vaccine sales plus ~$0.6B deferred revenue recognized related to Gavi (FY2023 10-K).
- Total revenue (XBRL, `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax`, USD, FY): $19.263B (2022, fact 2606780), $6.848B (2023, fact 2606789), $3.236B (2024, fact 2606798), accession 0001682852-25-000022. Derived YoY: **−64.4% in 2023** and **−52.7% in 2024** (calculations, not disclosed figures).
- 2024 drivers: lower volumes in Europe/rest of world as advance purchase agreements wound down; U.S. sales roughly flat only because of an **~$216M reversal of prior-year sales provisions** — excluding it, U.S. volume declined on lower vaccination rates and increased competition (FY2024 10-K, Item 7, chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:443872). Cost of sales fell 69% and dropped to 47% of net product sales from 70% in 2023, helped by the 2023 manufacturing resizing (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:447010).
- Outlook (forward-looking, not results): product sales expected to decline further in 2025 on lower vaccination rates, fewer remaining APAs and increasing competitive pressure (chunk 1682852/mrna-20241231:445227).

**Summary:** Moderna's vaccines moved from government-dominated pandemic purchasing to a seasonal, fragmented private market. Its U.S. COVID retail share rose from 37% (fall 2022) to 48% (fall 2023) but declined in 2024 amid intensified competition, while RSV share remained behind Pfizer and GSK. Revenue fell sharply in both 2023 and 2024.

**Limitations:** Only FY2023 and FY2024 10-Ks are bundled; no 2024 market-share percentage, unit volumes, or competitor share figures are disclosed, and the database has no product-level sales XBRL tag (product sales figures come from report text). Forward-looking statements are plans/expectations, not realized outcomes.
